items.context: Round 1 decided on a modal/dialog overlay (d1=B), but the brand-manager UI has NO reusable modal component — only native confirm() is used for delete. We need to build a modal from scratch. The question is how to implement it.

options.label: Custom Tailwind modal (inline in DiscoveryModal.tsx)
options.rationale: Build a simple backdrop + centered panel using Tailwind classes directly in the DiscoveryModal component. No new dependencies. Includes: fixed inset-0 backdrop with bg-black/50, centered panel with max-w-2xl, Escape key listener, click-outside-to-close. Matches the existing pattern of keeping things simple (the codebase uses native confirm() rather than a library). Recommended because this is the only modal in the app and adding a dependency for one use is overkill.

options.label: Radix UI Dialog primitive
options.rationale: Adds @radix-ui/react-dialog (~8KB). Gets accessible focus trapping, portal rendering, and animation support for free. The codebase already uses Radix patterns (Button uses Radix Slot). But adds a dependency for a single modal — may be worth it if more modals are planned.

options.label: HTML <dialog> element
options.rationale: Native browser dialog with showModal()/close() API. Built-in backdrop, Escape handling, and focus trapping. No dependencies. But styling the native ::backdrop is limited, and the imperative API (showModal/close) doesn't fit React's declarative model cleanly.

items.context: The discovery results are fairly rich: confidence badge, source table (up to 5 rows), draft brand preview (identity, colors, typography), and suggestions. All of this needs to fit in a modal overlay without feeling cramped. The modal needs to handle: initial state (input only), loading, error, and results.

options.label: Single scrollable panel with stacked sections
options.rationale: Vertically stack all result sections in a scrollable modal body: confidence badge at top, then source table, then draft preview (using Section component wrappers), then suggestions. max-h-[80vh] with overflow-y-auto. Simple, matches existing Section-based layout pattern used on all pages. Recommended because it's the simplest approach and the content volume is manageable (5 sources max, ~6 color swatches, a few text fields).

options.label: Tabbed view within modal
options.rationale: Three tabs: 'Overview' (confidence + summary), 'Sources' (detailed table), 'Preview' (draft brand). Reduces scroll depth but adds tab navigation complexity and may hide important context behind clicks.

options.label: Expandable accordion sections
options.rationale: Each result area (sources, identity, colors, typography, suggestions) is a collapsible section. Compact by default, user expands what they care about. Adds interaction overhead — user may miss important details if sections stay collapsed.

items.context: Discovery can return a result with zero sources and low/zero confidence if a scenario has no branding signals at all. We need to decide how to present this case, since the user might discover a scenario that has no branding elements.

options.label: Show empty state with 'No branding found' message and suggest creating from scratch
options.rationale: Display a friendly message like 'No branding elements found in {scenario}. You can create a brand from scratch instead.' with a button linking to the new brand form. Clear, actionable, and doesn't dead-end the user. Recommended because it keeps the flow moving.

options.label: Show partial results even with zero confidence, highlighting gaps
options.rationale: Still show the sources table (all empty) and suggestions (all as gaps). Informative but may feel like a cluttered 'nothing found' screen.

items.context: Modals need accessibility handling: focus trapping (so Tab doesn't escape behind the modal), aria attributes, and Escape key to close. The level of effort varies by approach.

options.label: Minimal: aria-modal, role='dialog', Escape handler, auto-focus first input
options.rationale: Covers the essentials: screen readers know it's a dialog, Escape closes it, first input gets focus on open. No focus trapping (Tab can escape to browser chrome). Good enough for an internal tool with limited modal usage. Recommended for pragmatism — this is the only modal in the app.

options.label: Full: above + focus trap (manual or via focus-trap library)
options.rationale: Proper focus trapping keeps Tab cycling within the modal. More accessible but requires either a small library (focus-trap-react, ~3KB) or manual implementation tracking focusable elements. Worth it if accessibility is a priority.

items.text: BrandFormPage's pre-fill integration is straightforward: the existing `brandToForm()` helper can convert a `Brand` object (from discovery's `draft_brand`) directly to `FormState`. The modification is minimal — add a `useEffect` that checks sessionStorage on mount, before the existing edit-mode effect runs. Since `emptyForm` is the default state, the pre-fill just overwrites it on mount.

Vitest + Testing Library is already fully configured in the brand-manager UI (vitest 2.1.4, @testing-library/react 16.1.0, jsdom). Existing component tests follow a consistent pattern (render, screen queries, fireEvent, vi.fn mocking). No additional test infrastructure setup is needed for the React tests decided in round 1.
